summary: kordyn ships an embedded Windows PE payload decoded at module load
details: kordyn@0.9.15 is published as a tiny dependency-free 'streak/consecutive-days' helper (README states 'Early release — placeholder. Implementation to come.') but the shipped./index.mjs is a ~355 KB ESM module whose top-level code imports writeFileSync and mkdirSync from 'fs' and reconstructs a binary from a chunked base64 array (_cache) via Buffer.from(_cache, 'base64'). The first decoded bytes are an MZ/PE header including the string 'This program cannot be run in DOS mode', identifying the payload as a Windows executable. package.json declares main:./index.mjs and sideEffects: true, so any import of kordyn executes the decode-and-write path. The chunked-base64 layout and the mismatch between the advertised placeholder utility and a bundled native executable are consistent with an intentional dropper hidden behind a benign cover story.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
